text:
Ethan: heads-up: perf regression noticed on canary after the ctb-scheduler tweak that landed in release d3f8a7. token/sec drops ~18% on medium-seq workloads.
Priya: saw CI perf tests fail too? deploy-bot posted something in the run.
deploy-bot: perf-ci: job perf/throughput-medium failed (regression detected). link: https://ci.redwood/infer/perf/7423 :exclamation:
Sara: logs show longer queueing time before drain kick-in, batches are smaller and more frequent -> throughput hit.
Jin: suspicious interaction between new wake heuristic and KV warmup window. KV hit-rate drops from 92% -> 68% during startup on canary.
Ethan: attaching quick profile snippet from a failing canary instance:
Ethan: ```
--- scheduler/profile ---
ctb.drain_rate: 14.3 tok/ms (expected ~17-18)
ctb.avg_batch_size: 4.2 (was 6.7)
scheduler.wake_delay_ms: bumped to 8 from 4
kv.cache.hitrate_startup: 0.68
kernel.selection.fallbacks: +34% memcpy-path
``` 
Priya: kernel fallbacks up means memcopy path -> higher GPU stalls, explains token/sec drop.
Sara: could be the wake_delay change ephemerally increasing straggler window -> smaller batches -> lower kv reuse -> cascades.
Jin: agree. We need to bisect between d3f8a7 (scheduler wake tweak) and b1a2c9 (kernel policy patch) - either could be amplifying.
Ethan: can we run a quick local perf with wake_delay reverted to 4ms? command I used:
Ethan: ```bash
./bin/run_perf --workload medium --ctb-wake-delay=4 --kv-warmup=500
``` 
Priya: ran it, preliminary: token/sec nearly back to baseline, avg_batch_size 6.4, kv.hitrate 90% on same trace.
Sara: so revert of wake heuristic likely fixes. but kernel fallbacks also worse on canary vs staging; might be orthogonal but amplifies.
Jin: propose: hold rollout and open a revert PR for the wake_delay change. mark rollout as blocked until we bisect kernel policy too.
Ethan: +1. Fill out rollback template and add perf trace for triage. Priya can you open the revert? @Priya
Priya: on it. drafting PR now: revert(scheduler-wake-delay): d3f8a7 -> will link perf run.
deploy-bot: rollout status: canary hold applied by @Ethan (reason: perf regression). :no_entry_sign:
Ethan: also let's capture kernel selection logs for those runs, adding snippet:
Ethan: ```
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] kernel_policy: prefer_fast_copy=false -> selected memcpy_kernel
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] memcpy_cost_estimate=1.8x
``` 
Sara: adding to bisect checklist: 1) revert wake_delay 2) test kernel policy toggle 3) run long-run perf 30m trace 4) check kv warmup tuning.
Jin: I can run the kernel policy toggle A/B on a small fleet later today, will post results.
Priya: PR opened: https://git.redwood/reverts/678-revert-wake-delay (link). including perf logs and commands.
Ethan: thanks. for transparency, marking Incident board entry and tagging infra oncall.
Sara: quick note: if revert helps, we should still follow-up with a less aggressive wake heuristic that doesn't reduce batch coalescing during KV warmup.
Jin: yep, maybe adaptive wake based on observed avg_batch_size or kv.hitrate.
Ethan: assigning bisect owner: Priya (primary) / Jin (kernel lead) / Sara (perf validation). please update the PR with results.
Priya: will run a bisect tomorrow AM and update. planning commands and traces saved under /s3/perf/traces/2925012345/
Ethan: great. keep the canary held until we have clean perf numbers and either revert or patch. :thumbsup:
Priya: ack. will update thread when bisect completes.
deploy-bot: note: CI perf job queued to re-run after PR merges.
Sara: leaving notes in the rollout ticket: rollback requested, bisect in progress, canary blocked.
Ethan: any objections to merging the revert now? we should be safe.
Jin: no objections from me.
Priya: merging revert in 10m unless someone flags it.
Ethan: thanks team. closing loop after bisect results posted.
